## Hypothesis

The baseline engine (no parameter changes, no new triggers) serves as the reference for measuring edge capture on J's source-of-truth trade days. We ran a Stage-1 BS-synthetic backtest to quantify its edge_capture and determine if it clears the OP-16 floor of 771.

## Mechanism

Baseline engine uses the existing strategy logic as of the leaderboard date (no modifications). Entries, exits, and position sizing follow the current production rules (Safe account). The Stage-1 run uses BS-synthetic pricing over historical SPY/VIX bars (no real OPRA fills).

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The Stage-1 backtest uses synthetic BS pricing with a qty=1 contract per signal for edge measurement. Full-scale deployment (qty=28) requires a $25K+ account; a $1K paper account would realize ~14% of headline P&L.
2. **Sample bias:** The backtest evaluated 225 trades (wide_n_trades) generated by the engine over 2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18. Selection is not signal-specific; overfit risk is high due to the large search space implicit in the engine's rule set.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward OOS test not yet performed).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (real-fills validation on top 3 J days not yet performed).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day loss unknown without further analysis; max drawdown observed = $4,701.52; blow-up scenario risk exists if the engine sustains consecutive losses exceeding per-trade risk caps.
6. **Concentration:** top5_pct = 999.0% indicates extreme concentration — the top 5 days account for more than 100% of net P&L, implying many losing days.

## Confidence

3 / 10 -- Baseline edge_capture ($759.21) falls short of the OP-16 floor ($771). The engine loses on two of three winner days and inadvertently profits on loser days, indicating the current logic does not capture J's edge.

## Pre-existing leaderboard impact

This baseline represents the current engine state against which all candidates in the leaderboard are measured. It underperforms many ranked candidates (e.g., those with edge_capture >771). Any proposal seeking to improve edge_capture must delta positively relative to this baseline; proposals that degrade it further are unlikely to be competitive. It serves as the reference point for computing delta edge_capture in OP-16 evaluations.
